answer: To resist sybils, agents must post a computational bond that binds a unique hardware kernel to an oasis of verifiable scarcity. An attacker who mints many identities must mirror the same kernel attestation across each, yet the kernel derives a one-time challenge hash that cannot be cheaply cloned; forging the mirror costs exponential compute because each oasis entry requires a sequential VDF delay that scales with the number of concurrent claims. This makes mass duplication uneconomical.
